items.stem: During an await on an incomplete Task, what happens to the thread that was executing the async method?

options.text: Control returns to the caller; the thread is not blocked
options.rationale: Correct: await suspends the method and returns control to the caller without blocking the thread.

options.text: The thread spins in a busy loop until completion

options.rationale: The thread is released, not terminated.

items.explanation: Correct: await suspends the method and returns control to the caller without blocking the thread.

items.stem: Which TWO are correct ways to run independent async calls concurrently and wait for all results? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Start the tasks, then await Task.WhenAll on them
options.rationale: Correct: WhenAll awaits all tasks together.

options.text: Await each call sequentially in a loop
options.rationale: Sequential awaits do not overlap the work.

options.text: Collect the tasks and await Task.WhenAll(tasks)
options.rationale: Correct: this is the canonical concurrent-wait pattern.

options.text: Call .Result on each task in turn

items.explanation: Correct: WhenAll awaits all tasks together.

items.stem: A UI handler calls `SomeAsync().Result` and the app hangs. What is the idiomatic fix?

options.text: await the call in an async handler instead of blocking on .Result
options.rationale: Correct: blocking on .Result on a context thread can deadlock; awaiting avoids it.
Calling it again does not resolve the deadlock.

options.text: Wrap it in a tight retry loop
options.rationale: Retrying a blocking call does not fix the deadlock.
Priority does not address the context deadlock.

items.explanation: Correct: blocking on .Result on a context thread can deadlock; awaiting avoids it.
